title.value: What Can Machine Learning Do for Psychiatry?
title.justification: This is explicitly stated as the title of one of the sections in the research paper.
title.quote: What Can Machine Learning Do for Psychiatry? Daniel Barron ^{1} , Danilo Bzdok ^{2} , John H. Krystal ^{1} , and R. Todd Constable ^{1}

analysis.description: The paper surveys the application of Machine Learning (ML) in psychiatry, analyzing both quantitative trends and qualitative features across 2,058 published abstracts. The study uses ML to identify patterns in psychiatric research and discusses the broad range of features and target variables explored in these studies.

type.justification: The paper involves a systematic quantitative and qualitative survey of published literature, applying machine learning techniques such as k-means clustering and latent-factor decomposition, and thus qualifies as empirical research.
type.quote: To assess how ML relates neurobiology to clinically observed phenomena, we performed a systematic quantitative and qualitative survey of the published literature.

name.justification: The paper focuses on applying machine learning within the field of psychiatry, assessing neurobiological data related to clinical observations in mental health.
name.quote: Machine learning (ML) algorithms are increasingly advertised as a paradigm-shifting way forward in mental health research and clinical care.

name.justification: The study highlights the use of machine learning techniques to analyze psychiatric data.
name.quote: Advances ML algorithms might derive data-driven, novel features or target variables from neurobiological data.

name.justification: K-means clustering is explicitly mentioned as a method used in the research study for deriving word-occurrence clusters.
name.quote: We then used k-means clustering to automatically derive 10 word-occurrence clusters, producing summary terms for each cluster.

is_contributed.justification: K-means clustering is a well-established machine learning method and not a new contribution by this paper.
is_contributed.quote: We then used k-means clustering to automatically derive 10 word-occurrence clusters.
